cheng: Heads-up — need to backport a docs-only change to 1.4.x. Deploybot says it will auto-bump. Is this worth a patch bump during the 02:00-04:00 UTC change window?

deploy-bot: [automated] deploybot check: PR #4321 (docs-only). suggested_bump: patch. window_ok: true. notes: no binaries changed.

maria: docs-only -> usually prefer buildmeta so we don't churn patch counts. buildmeta like `v1.4.3+docs.1` keeps semver intent.

alex: +1 for buildmeta if tooling tolerates it. patch triggers release-notes flow and some customers pin patches.

sam: fwiw Dedicated customers pin to exact patch. If we do buildmeta they won't receive it unless they unpin. So consider impact on clients.

ritesh: ops perspective: if we ship during the window, patch is safer for customer expectations. If we choose patch, add a short "docs backport" release note and mark as non-functional.

cheng: tradeoff noted. My leaning: because deploybot will tag and our deploy workflows expect semantic bumps for backports, do a patch. Example tag we can use:
```
# tag locally
git tag -a v1.4.3 -m "docs: clarify example in quickstart (backport)"
git push origin v1.4.3
```

maria: if we go patch, run minimal changelog emit to avoid noise: `./scripts/release/emit-changelog --scope=docs --quiet`

alex: also add release metadata: `labels: [docs,backport,nonfunctional]` and `rollback: quick` so SRE can act fast if anything unexpected.

sam: can we delay the push to 03:30 UTC? earlier in the window still has higher traffic.

cheng: ok hold until 03:30, I'll do tagging then and add the blurb: "docs backport — no runtime changes" to the release notes.

deploy-bot: [automated] scheduled release pending: v1.4.3 by cheng at 03:30 UTC. prechecks: ok.

deploy-bot: [automated] release v1.4.3 pushed at 03:31 UTC by cheng — status: succeeded :tada:

cheng: :thumbsup:
